items.followUp: Why do passengers jerk backward when a bus starts suddenly?

rubric.why: Checks identification of inertia of motion as the relevant principle.
rubric.how: Award for naming inertia of motion as the cause.

rubric.why: Checks how inertia causes the passenger to move forward relative to the braking bus.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that the feet slow with the bus while the upper body tends to continue moving forward.

modelAnswer: When the driver applies the brakes suddenly, the bus and the passengers’ feet slow down.
Because of inertia of motion, the upper part of the passengers’ bodies tends to keep moving forward, so they fall forward.
